en: A wise person does not tell others about loss of money, pain in his mind, his wife's conduct, rude words said by low people, or an insult he has suffered.
One who sets shyness aside in dealing with money and grain, in gaining knowledge, in eating, and in business will be happy.
The happiness and peace of those filled with the nectar of contentment is never known to the greedy, who run here and there for money.
Be content with three things: your own wife, your food and your wealth; but never be content with three: study, prayer and giving.
Do not walk between two Brahmins, between a Brahmin and the fire, between husband and wife, between master and servant, or between a plough and its ox.

first: पादाभ्यां न स्पृशेदग्नि गुरुं ब्राह्मणमेव च ।
en: Never touch with your feet fire, a teacher, a Brahmin, a cow, a young girl, an old person or a child.
Keep a thousand arm-lengths from an elephant, a hundred from a horse, ten from a horned animal; but to avoid a wicked man, leave the country.
An elephant is controlled with a goad, a horse with the hand, a horned animal with a stick, and a wicked man with a sword.
Brahmins are pleased by a good meal, peacocks by thunder, good people by others' good fortune, and wicked people by others' trouble.
Win a strong person by going along with him, a wicked one by opposing him, and an enemy of equal strength by politeness or by force.
A king's strength is the power of his arms, a Brahmin's strength is knowledge of God, and a woman's greatest strength is her beauty, youth and sweetness.
Do not be too straight; go and look at a forest: there the straight trees are cut down, and the crooked ones are left standing.
Swans live where there is water and leave when it dries up; a person should not be like the swan, leaving and coming back again and again.

first: उपार्जितानां वित्तानां त्याग एव हि रक्षणम् ।
en: Spending wealth you have earned is the way to protect it, just as water flowing out of a tank keeps it fresh.
One who has money has friends and relatives; he is counted a man in the world, and he alone is said to truly live.
People who have come from heaven carry four signs in their body in this world: love of giving, sweet speech, worship of the gods, and feeding the learned.
Great anger, harsh speech, poverty, hatred toward one's own people, company of the low, and serving the base are signs of those who have come from hell.
If you go to a lion's den you may find a pearl from an elephant's head; but if you go to a jackal's den you will find only a calf's tail and scraps of donkey hide.
Life without learning is as useless as a dog's tail, which can neither cover its private parts nor drive away biting insects.
Purity of speech, purity of mind, control of the senses and kindness to all beings: this is the purity of those who seek the highest goal.

first: पुष्पे गन्धतिले तैलं काष्ठे वह्नि पयो घृतम् ।
en: As there is scent in a flower, oil in sesame, fire in wood, butter in milk and sugar in cane, so with clear thinking see the soul within the body.
